claims.text: Elevated temperature enhances interfacial atomic mobility in FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers.
Enhanced interfacial atomic mobility induces chemical intermixing across FCC/BCC interfaces.
Chemical intermixing erodes short-range order at FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy interfaces.
Interfacial short-range order acts as a barrier to dislocation nucleation and slip.
Loss of interfacial short-range order lowers the energy barrier for dislocation nucleation.
Intermixing and short-range-order degradation prompt a transition from dislocation-dominated to diffusion-assisted creep.
The proposed change in creep mechanism produces progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading.
Thermal pretreatment can establish distinct initial short-range-order states in the multilayers.
Quenching produces relatively high short-range order, whereas annealing produces relatively low short-range order.
Near-room-temperature creep testing inhibits interfacial diffusion relative to moderately elevated-temperature testing.
A diffusion-barrier variant minimizes interfacial diffusion and can serve as a control.
Mechanical stress acts together with compositional intermixing to disrupt local interfacial short-range order.
Reduced interfacial order facilitates dislocation slip.
Elevated-temperature samples will develop greater interfacial compositional gradients than low-temperature or diffusion-inhibited controls.
Elevated-temperature samples will exhibit reduced interfacial short-range order.
Elevated-temperature samples will exhibit greater interfacial dislocation activity than low-temperature or diffusion-inhibited controls.
Elevated-temperature samples will have lower creep resistance than low-temperature or diffusion-inhibited controls.
Multilayers with minimal interfacial diffusion and intact short-range order have higher creep resistance.
Multilayers with intact short-range order possess well-defined barriers to dislocation motion.
The proposed mechanism applies only while diffusion is significant but remains below the onset of catastrophic phase mixing and while competing failure modes are inactive.
